perspective:
From Ethan Mohamud’s perspective, he has access to:

- He is Ethan, a plumber, and Gary Guo is his close, long-time friend since middle school; Gary is a doctor.
- He noticed Gary working excessively long hours at the hospital, skipping meals, and sacrificing sleep. He became concerned and invited Gary to a two-day weekend retreat, saying Gary’s health matters and he hated seeing him like this. He heard Gary initially refuse, saying he appreciated the concern but couldn’t because there was too much to do at the hospital.
- At the retreat, Ethan observed Gary acting restless and avoiding discussions about work. Ethan suspected there was more to Gary’s overworking than professional obligations. He confronted Gary, reminding him of their middle-school friendship and saying Gary could tell him anything and that he was there to help, not judge. Gary replied that it was complicated and he didn’t want to burden Ethan.
- After that, Gary opened up to Ethan about pressures from managing a new department and personal challenges he was facing. Ethan felt relief and empathy and suggested prioritizing tasks and delegating responsibilities. Gary agreed and said he could use help organizing his schedule to make time for himself.
- Over the following months, Ethan regularly checked in with Gary. He saw Gary making efforts to change and felt hopeful and proud. Gary told him things were better, he was less overwhelmed because of Ethan’s help, and he had had time for a movie the previous weekend.
- After a year, Ethan saw Gary managing on his own and believed Gary had things under control. Ethan felt satisfied and happy and decided to step back, while telling Gary he was always a call away and knew Gary had it. Gary thanked him, said he couldn’t have done it without Ethan’s support, and felt more in control.

Ethan does not have access to hidden hospital events, private details Gary never told him, or narrator-only conclusions beyond what he observed or was told.
